title: Buffer Zone Map: Setback and Exclusion Zones
description: Create a circular buffer at any distance with the Buffer Zone Map — planning setbacks, exclusion zones and reach rings on a live map. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 35 ft setback buffer around a 50 ft-radius pond creates a protected ring of approx. 14,844 sq ft (0.34 acres) where the two circles' areas differ.
quick_answer: The Buffer Zone Map draws a circular buffer at a chosen distance around a point. Set the centre, pick the buffer distance, and inspect the ring — the working picture behind planning setbacks, exclusion zones around sensitive sites, and reach questions a bare radius does not frame.

Spray drift, noise and habitat protection all draw buffers. The map turns a number in a guidance document into the area it actually governs.
Crane swings, blasting radii and site compounds are planned as buffers around a point. A drawn ring briefs a crew faster than a paragraph.
Who must be notified, consulted or evacuated within X of a site? The buffer ring is the list's boundary — addresses inside it are the answer.

Pond radius approx. 50 ft; a 35 ft setback ring around it spans radii 50–85 ft, an area of π × (85² − 50²) ≈ 14,844 sq ft (0.34 acres). That ring — not the pond — is the land the setback actually removes from use.
A 500 m buffer around a proposed site covers π × 500² ≈ 78.5 hectares of neighbourhood. The area figure is why notification duties are written in distances, not in 'nearby'.

faq: Is a buffer the same as a radius circle?
Geometrically yes — the difference is intent. A radius measures reach; a buffer declares a zone with a rule attached (setback, exclusion, notification). The drawing is shared, the meaning is yours.
This tool draws the straight-line (geodesic) buffer — the kind regulations are written in. Road-based reach is a different shape; the Drive Time Map draws that one.
Can I use this for service-area planning?
Yes, as the geographic screen: the ring defines the candidate area. Population, roads and rules then refine it — the tool's job is the honest boundary.
Are map measurements legal survey measurements?
No. A drawn buffer is a planning picture at map accuracy. A setback with legal consequences is staked by survey, not by satellite image.
What distance units can I use?
Feet, metres, miles and kilometres — buffers are specified in all four depending on the regulation's country. US examples here use feet; European ones metres.
Can I buffer a line or an area, not just a point?
This tool buffers a point into a disc. Buffers around roads and parcels are polygon operations — draw the feature's outline in the acreage tools and offset thinking starts there.
Why does the area grow so fast?
Area scales with the square of distance. The table on this page is the antidote to the intuition that doubling a setback 'only' doubles its effect.
How is a buffer around a point different from one around a road?
A point buffer is a disc. A road buffer is a capsule — the road's line thickened by the distance, with round caps — which needs line geometry this point tool does not draw.
Yes, and where setbacks from two features overlap, the union of the rings is the governed land. The Equal Circle Overlap Calculator sizes the shared lens of two equal discs.
